correctness.rationale: Both exact equations check by cancellation. The homogeneous second equation reduces the first to a standard Sylvester equation with eigenvalues on circles of radii 1 and r=(1+τ)^(-1/n)<1, ensuring uniqueness. Input matrices have κ2≤2. Both solutions are ±I, so all singular values are 1; the projector pair yields explicit residual matrices with squared Frobenius norms 2 and 0, first equation denominator 2√k+2, and squared relative forward error (n-k)/n. For n=m²,k=m the limiting result is rigorous. The 1035 finite Fraction checks supplement rather than prove the universal statement.

originality.rationale: The primary and classical literature were compared at the level of mathematical implications. Standard rank-one displacement and rank-one Sylvester forcing with flat solution singular values are explicitly prior art. The distinct combined theorem adds two simultaneously nonzero rank-one coupled forcings, condition-number ≤2 coefficients and disjoint generalized spectra, and a quantitative sequence where the specific published normalized residual tends to zero while forward errors tend to one. Accessible primary sections and semantic database searches have not identified direct coverage; historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Classical displacement-structure texts may contain an equivalent coupled example under a different formulation.
The Beckermann–Townsend full manuscript and Jarlebring–Mele full manuscript were not read in entirety; neither abstract alone supports exclusion.
Semantic database ranking cannot prove global scientific priority.
The normalized residual construction exploits near-resonance; uniform separation would substantially change the question.

value.rationale: The exact benchmark tests a natural research question about when coupled low-rank equation data and apparently successful termwise-normalized residuals justify low-rank solution recovery. It shows a quantitative, asymptotically decisive failure without allowing poor conditioning of individual coefficient matrices, and isolates the missing dimension-uniform spectral separation/low-rank-solution hypothesis. It is not an arbitrary single size or mere computed example; it provides an all-dimensional limit and an exact diagnostic formula, suitable as a stress test for low-rank solver stopping criteria.
